pages.title: Black-crowned Night Heron
pages.summary: Tame it with raw cod or salmon for a companion that occasionally brings you a fish.

spans.text: Hold raw cod, raw salmon, tropical fish or pufferfish, then sneak forward slowly. Do not sprint right up to it. It can notice fish in either your main hand or off hand.

Holding fish makes it less wary of you; sprinting makes it more wary. Individual temperament, distance and recent scares also affect its response. If it has started backing away or preparing to fly, stop and give it space.
Drop raw fish onto stable ground nearby. If the heron is awake, grounded and not fleeing, it walks over, picks up the fish and swallows it. Eating dropped fish does not trigger taming.

Raw cod, raw salmon, tropical fish and pufferfish can attract it or be fed on the ground; cooked fish cannot. It may pick up fish contaminated with droppings, spit it out, and stop collecting food for a while.

sections.title: Taming with raw cod or salmon

spans.text: Hold clean raw cod or raw salmon and right-click the heron. Each accepted feeding consumes one fish and has a default 1/3 chance to tame it. Tropical fish, pufferfish, cooked fish and fish contaminated with droppings cannot tame it.

Wait until it finishes handling any fish in its beak, eating, or reacting to contaminated food. Once tamed, it switches to Follow. Its owner can feed it more raw cod or salmon to restore one heart. Night herons cannot breed.

As the owner, sneak and right-click with both hands empty to cycle through Free, Follow, Stay and Return to Nest. Raw cod or salmon in your off hand takes priority for feeding. Either hand can feed it; leave your main hand empty when using the off hand. Return to Nest looks for a nearby perch. Changing modes preserves any fish in its beak.

Follow mode stays active during the day. While you move, the heron alternates between following on foot and brief circling flights. When you stop, it looks for a safe nearby landing spot within interaction range. It flies over from a distance without teleporting. Choose Stay or Return to Nest to keep it in place. The 32-block gift range does not limit ordinary following.
Once tamed, a heron in Free or Follow mode may bring its owner a fish. No assigned task, pond, bank, fishing rod or live fish is needed.

By default, it tries after every 5–10 minutes of eligible active time, with a 50% chance to place one raw cod or salmon directly in its beak and bring it to its owner. It carries at most one fish. An unsuccessful attempt waits for the next interval.

The heron carries its fish to its owner, lands safely, pauses briefly and places the fish on the ground in front of them. In Follow mode, it resumes accompanying its owner after delivery. You can also right-click it within three blocks with an empty main hand, without sneaking, to collect the fish directly into your inventory.

If your inventory is full and has no matching fish stack with room, the heron keeps holding the fish. Free some space and right-click with an empty hand. Do not sneak, as that changes its companion command.

The gift timer advances while the heron is safe and awake at dusk or nighttime, with its owner online, in the same dimension and within 32 blocks by default. Following during the day does not advance gift time. Offline time, rest, Stay and Return to Nest pause the timer.

No new fish is generated while its beak is occupied. Reloading preserves a carried fish and the remaining wait; time spent offline does not generate extra gifts. Bird-watching settings let you disable gifts or adjust the owner range and attempt intervals.

At dusk and at night, it looks for fish in the water along the bank and stretches its neck to catch them when they are close enough. It needs nearby water, a bank it can stand on, and the willingness to forage. It does not keep fishing when full or frightened.

A wild heron’s alarm response progresses through freezing to observe, backing away, running, low flight and long-distance flight. Repeated chasing builds up fear and may also startle nearby wild herons.
A tamed heron does not flee merely because an ordinary player approaches or wild birds nearby become frightened. It still avoids danger when attacked.
During the day, it rests on sheltered banks or near vegetation. Attacks and loud noises can wake it. It can use a water- or fish-filled
, but will not come over immediately if it is sleeping, fleeing or eating a fish.
Raw cod, raw salmon, tropical fish and pufferfish.

spans.text: Look for sparrows on the ground near villages and farmland. Hold seeds to attract their attention, keep your distance and wait for them to approach. A recently hurt sparrow that is still avoiding players will not respond normally to an approach.

Hold clean seeds and right-click. Each attempt consumes one item and gives a wild sparrow a 1/3 chance of being tamed. Feeding a tamed sparrow restores a little health. Adults enter love mode when the breeding conditions are met.
to scatter a food pile on supported ground. Nearby sparrows will approach and peck at it. Ground feeding and right-click taming with held seeds are separate actions.

Hold the camera and right-click to open the viewfinder. Left-click to take a photo. Right-click or press Esc to exit.

pages.title: Bird baths
pages.summary: Adding water and food, collecting rain, freezing, and cleaning across all six bird baths.

spans.text: Wood, stone, and iron each have two styles, for six versions in total. Capacity, cleaning, and weather mechanics are the same.

Place the bath on the top face of a block. Right-click with a water bucket to fill all three units, leaving an empty bucket. A water bottle adds one unit and leaves a glass bottle. Empty any food from the bath before adding water.
Right-click while holding a supported food. Each item adds one unit, up to three. You can top up the same food type; adding a different type replaces the contents. Different types cannot be mixed.
Accepts cod and salmon (raw or cooked), tropical fish, and pufferfish; beef, pork, mutton, chicken, and rabbit (raw or cooked); bread or breadcrumbs.
The bath must have a clear view of the sky while it is raining. Empty baths and water-filled baths automatically fill to three units of water. Rain does not replace food or ice.
Rain has a chance to remove one level of dirt, but will not wash away spoiled contents. A roof or other cover stops rain collection.
Water has a chance to freeze if the bath is open to the sky and its biome is cold enough for snow. A frozen bath cannot provide normal drinking or bathing water for birds.

Thawing also requires an open sky. Ice has a chance to melt during the day once the environment is no longer cold enough. Periodic checks trigger these changes, so they are not immediate. Right-click a frozen bath with a water bucket to replace the ice with a full bath of water. A water bottle can also add water and thaw a partially filled frozen bath.

Fish and meat have a base spoilage time of 60 minutes; bread takes 120 minutes. Time accumulates while the chunk is running. Food spoils faster outdoors during dry daylight hours. Successfully adding food restarts the timer. Right-clicking a full bath consumes no food and does not reset the timer.
Spoiled contents display a decay effect and must be cleared with an empty hand. Adding water or waiting for rain will not remove them.
Bird use and water left standing make the bath dirty. At the highest dirt level, birds cannot properly drink, eat, or bathe. The bath needs cleaning even if it still has contents.

Right-click with an empty hand to improve cleanliness by one level. If the contents are spoiled, the first action removes them; dirt remains and needs further cleaning. Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to empty the bath. Spoiled contents are removed first if present.

Using a water bucket on an empty, partially water-filled, or frozen bath also improves cleanliness by one level if the bath is at its dirtiest. An outdoor water bath has a chance to lose one unit to evaporation during dry daylight hours. Breaking the bath does not return its water or food.

Birds naturally shed feathers about every 10–20 minutes when a player is nearby and molting conditions are met. Otherwise, the check is postponed. Killing birds does not drop feathers.

pages.title: Bird droppings
pages.summary: Can be thrown, used as fertilizer or compost, or made into prank food.

spans.text: Birds leave stains after defecating. Right-click a stain with a brush to clean it and receive a random type of bird droppings, using 1 brush durability. Outside Creative mode, breaking a stain also drops a random type of droppings.
All four types share these uses. Their main differences are stain appearance and the chances of fertilizing crops or adding compost. Collecting a stain does not guarantee a particular type.

Aim into the air, hold right-click for at least 0.15 seconds, then release. A longer charge throws farther, reaching full charge after about 1 second. Each throw consumes 1 item, with a 0.5-second interval. Droppings disappear in water.
Hitting most mobs or players inflicts about 4 seconds of Slowness. Some mobs have special reactions. Hitting a suitable surface leaves a stain that can be cleaned and collected again.
Place droppings in a dispenser and trigger it with redstone. All four types can be fired. Each shot consumes 1 item and travels in the direction the dispenser faces.

In your inventory's 2×2 crafting grid or a crafting table, place 1 of any bird dropping and 1 food item or potion in any arrangement. The grid must contain only these two ingredients. The recipe produces 1
. Already contaminated items cannot be processed again.
Drop food or a potion on the ground, then throw droppings at it. A direct hit or a nearby impact turns 1 item into prank food; it does not contaminate the whole stack at once.
The item keeps its original texture, but one character in its name changes. Eating or drinking it gives Nausea for 8 seconds, Hunger for 8 seconds, and Slowness for 3 seconds.
Place a cake on the ground, then hit it with thrown droppings. The cake is marked as contaminated. Players who eat it receive the negative effects of prank food.
An unplaced cake item cannot be crafted with droppings like bread can.

Hold droppings and right-click a farmland block to check crops in a 3×3 area centered on it. Each dropping type has a different chance of success, and the crop must also pass its own bone meal growth check.
Click the farmland, not the crop. Nothing is consumed if there are no eligible crops nearby. If an eligible crop is present, one item is consumed even if no growth occurs.
Hold droppings and right-click a composter. Each item has a type-specific chance of raising the compost level by one.
Wolf  /  Brief Slowness and whimpering. Tamed wolves look at their owner. Nearby seagulls may mimic the sound.
Cat  /  Hisses, briefly speeds up, and moves away.
Fox  /  Is startled, with an additional 15% chance of dropping one item from its mouth.
Skeleton variants  /  About 2 seconds of Slowness and 3.5 seconds of Weakness.
Enderman  /  Attempts to teleport and targets the thrower or a nearby player for attack.
Villager  /  When hit by a player, temporarily raises trade prices for about 3 minutes. Repeated hits increase the surcharge.
Iron golem  /  In Survival mode, hitting it 3 times within one minute causes it to retaliate.
Hitting a pressure plate produces a redstone pulse lasting 1 second by default. The server configuration controls this feature and its duration.

pages.title: UwU Funk Music Disc
pages.summary: Plays in a jukebox, attracting nearby pigeons to approach and dance.

spans.text: Available in the Creative inventory. The current local build has no Survival crafting recipe or drops configured.
Hold the disc and right-click an empty jukebox to insert it. The music attracts pigeons within 16 blocks. They dance after approaching to about 3 blocks and stop when playback ends.
Right-click the jukebox again to remove the disc. After a server restart, remove and reinsert it to trigger playback and dancing again. The track is about two minutes long.

Geese, eagles, seagulls, swallows, cranes, vultures and starling flocks appear in the distant sky according to biome, time and weather. They are client-side ambient effects, not entities you can feed, catch or tame.

pages.title: Hummingbird
pages.summary: A tiny bird that hovers beside flowers, especially active in the morning. Wild hummingbirds also pollinate and occasionally bring back vanilla flowers; tamed birds can follow their owner.

facts.label: Activity
facts.text: Daytime / more active in the morning

facts.label: Habitat
facts.text: Flower forests / sunflower plains / meadows / savannas

spans.text: During the day, it hovers at flowers or sugar-water baths to feed. At other times in Free mode, it prefers tree canopies and branches, with more activity in the morning. It sleeps only in trees at night, so planting trees gives your garden a roost. Look in flower forests, sunflower plains, meadows and savannas. Natural spawning also requires at least five flowers within 16 blocks.
It has 4 health points (2 hearts). Approach gently rather than chasing or attacking it.

sections.title: Five feedings from the same player

spans.text: Hold honeycomb, sugar, poppies, red tulips, pink tulips, rose bushes or peonies and right-click to feed it. By default, five accepted feedings from the same player tame it. A different player starts a new count.

As its owner, sneak and right-click with both hands empty to cycle through Free, Follow, Stay and Return to Nest. Free mode visits suitable flowers and sugar-water baths. Stay and Return to Nest allow it to rest.

While following, it hovers around its owner and changes position from time to time. Once you stop, it may visit nearby flowers along the way. If you stay still and there is room above your head, it may perch there. With both hands empty, sneak and right-click safe ground to put it down in Stay mode.
Sneak while holding a flower and right-click your hummingbird to bind a nearby bird bath or a garden around the current location. Add flowers, replenish sugar water and let it roam freely.

Hummingbirds can turn quickly, move sideways and fly backwards. They approach a flower from the side, place their beak near its center, hover to drink and back away before moving on. Feeding does not consume the flower. Obstacles, danger or unsuitable targets cause them to search again.

Add sugar to a clean bird bath containing clean water to turn the current water level into sugar water. Each successful drink uses one serving; rain does not replenish it. Empty and clean dirty or spoiled baths before refilling.
Both wild and tamed hummingbirds become temporary pollination sources after effective nectar feeding. By default, they help wheat, carrots, potatoes and beetroot within eight blocks.

Every 20 seconds, each eligible crop receives one extra growth roll: 25% chance per active hummingbird, capped at four birds. This does not directly multiply vanilla random growth speed. Pollination is subject to server rules and permissions, including the mob-griefing rule.
Sleeping, danger, Stay mode and departure from the effective range stop ongoing benefits. Nothing runs in unloaded chunks and no offline rewards accumulate.

Hummingbirds do not need to be tamed to bring back vanilla flowers. Free activity advances their waiting time, and an actual completed flower visit is required for a chance to obtain one flower of the same type. A bird already carrying something cannot generate another item.
It carries the collected item to its bound bird bath or a nearby bath and drops it there. If it cannot find a bath, it keeps carrying the item until you provide a collection spot.
The gift is a regular vanilla flower item, which can be planted or used according to vanilla rules.
Budgerigars occasionally watch or take a few steps toward an active hummingbird. Cockatiels watch from where they stand. Existing owner commands, feeding, sleep and escape behavior take priority.

Free-roaming hummingbirds sometimes circle and chase one another without dealing damage. By default, a pair of males has a 20% chance to start a display; pairs involving a female have a 2% chance. Each opportunity is followed by a 120-second cooldown, while the chase itself lasts about 3–4 seconds.

A flower garden with hummingbirds actively feeding can increase local spawning weights for sparrows, long-tailed tits and crested mynas by up to 15% by default. Each species still follows its habitat restrictions, server settings and population caps.
